notes: This contract records Umbra's first bounded public timestamped service family in the non-installable IEEE 1516.1-2025 development profile: timestamped Send Interaction for non-regional interactions, with federation-owned queueing for time-constrained recipients, callback-gated delivery before Time Advance Grant, official timestamp/order/retraction callback fields, lower-bound validation from the sender's current or requested time plus lookahead, and pre-delivery Retract. The shared recipient planner selects active ordinary subscriptions only; passive ordinary subscriptions remain declared but do not arrange delivery, although the current timestamped cases do not independently test that selector. A callback-boundary ordinary unsubscribe terminally suppresses an accepted nonconstrained recipient without pretending it received the interaction or later Request Retraction. The separately checked request-retraction contract covers the deliberately bounded legal post-delivery normal interaction path and terminal-designator lifecycle. A focused regression advances the producer to the exact strict Retract boundary while the recipient's interaction remains queued: the callback still arrives, while the returned designator is retained as MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted after delivery. Connection Lost regressions retain queued payloads through a source-mandated loss cutoff at time 6: two exact-time cases cover a TAR pending at loss or submitted afterward, and a strict-less-than case delivers timestamp 5 before the survivor's grant to 6. A composite asynchronous-delivery case proves the exact time-6 boundary also appears in HLAreportFederateLost; none claims a result for a later timestamp. A separate one-federate regression proves that an eligible-recipient set of zero still yields a valid public designator backed by the lightweight federation ledger; it covers legal Retract and later terminal classification without retaining a typed interaction payload. A default-region companion now proves that a queued timestamped interaction survives a Time Constrained disable/re-enable cycle and still delivers once before its grant with the supplied-empty region marker. An ordinary non-regional companion now covers the same lifecycle boundary without DDM or a source-region realization, proving the joined-federate queue identity survives callback-gated Time Constrained re-enable and that one Receive Interaction callback still precedes the matching grant with the official metadata and terminal retraction classification. A second focused normal-interaction regression proves that Disable Time Regulation temporarily removes Retract authority without terminalizing a pending designator; callback-gated re-enable at unchanged lookahead restores authority for one legal Retract and later terminal classification. A companion now proves that an accepted queued TSO interaction is not discarded by that regulation-role transition and is delivered exactly once before the recipient's matching grant. A third save/restore regression restores a pre-save live queued interaction and retraction ledger after a post-save Retract made it terminal, then verifies original delivery and legal post-delivery Retract. One bounded ordinary non-regional interaction scenario now drives the same queued payload through Flush Queue Request, Time Advance Request Available, and Next Message Request Available recipients, proving callback-before-grant ordering, FQR actual/optimistic time, and official callback metadata. Voluntary-source-resignation companions now prove that an accepted non-regional TSO interaction remains queued after the producer invokes Resign Federation Execution with NO_ACTION for both a single survivor and two recipient-local queues: independent remaining regulators advance the survivors, which receive the original producer, timestamp, tag, order, parameter, and retraction metadata before their Time Advance Grants. This is bounded development-profile lifecycle evidence; other resignation actions, alternate advances, recovery, remote transport, package/JUnit/protected-review evidence, and conformance remain open. This contract still does not claim timestamped Update Attribute Values, Delete Object Instance, Send Directed Interaction, Send Interaction With Regions, a complete alternate-advance matrix beyond that ordinary frontier, broader Disable Time Regulation/re-enable boundaries, broader asynchronous-delivery behavior, request-retraction callbacks for other message families, durable and complete terminal save/restore recovery, remote transport, package support, catalog evidence, JUnit evidence, protected review, or conformance.

requirements.notes: The ordinary four-member case accepts one timestamp-6 Send Interaction for two constrained recipients, admits direct TAR(6) and NMR(10) while the producer regulator is present, then resigns the producer with NO_ACTION. Its default-region Restaurant FOM companion repeats the two-recipient lifecycle with explicit overlapping subscriber regions and a private default source realization. An independent regulator releases each recipient-local queue one at a time; every Receive Interaction callback retains the original payload, tag, producer, timestamp/order, supplied-empty region marker, and retraction metadata before its matching grant. requirements.notes: The mixed-family companion adds one timestamped interaction to the saved object-update image and proves that its recipient-local ledger restores independently before Flush Queue delivery and post-delivery Request Retraction. This is additive composition evidence, not a complete interaction/attribute save/restore or durable persistence claim.

The accepted timestamped §6.12 Send Interaction path uses the shared file-or-interaction selector after TSO admission assigns any message-retraction identity and before a queued Receive Interaction callback. The focused production-filesystem case proves type-27 InteractionClassHandle, type-40 ParameterHandleValueMap, type-63 User-supplied tag, and type-31 LogicalTime supplied forms, the type-34 Null returned argument for a non-time-regulating sender, serial zero, and durable report-before-callback ordering. The paired native HLA_IMMEDIATE case now proves the time-regulated type-33 MessageRetractionHandle return before the constrained callback with the same supplied forms and callback metadata. Regional/timestamped object-update/delete families, remote transport, and conformance remain separate; the Lab has no row-level backend relation (RL-105/RL-152), so this is development-profile traceability only.
